title: Bulk superconductivity in quintuple-layer square-planar nickelate La6Ni5O12
authors: Mengzhu Shi, Mei Du, Hongyu Li, Zhiwei Wang, Zhengjie Wang, Ziji Xiang, Tao Wu, Xianhui Chen
abstract: Nickelate superconductors, sharing a similar electronic environment with cuprate superconductors, offer a promising platform for unraveling the mechanism of high-temperature superconductivity. However, the realization of superconductivity in these systems has so far been restricted to thin films or bulk samples under high-pressure. This limits the applicability of various experimental probes to study the mechanism of superconductivity, and hinders the potential application of the nickelate superconductors. Exploring bulk superconductivity at ambient pressure is therefore essential to understand its origin and enable broader experimental research. Here, we report the realization of bulk superconductivity at ambient-pressure in quintuple-layer square-planar (SP) nickelate La6Ni5O12. The SP phase is obtained by performing topotactic reaction on the quintuple-layer Ruddlesden-Popper (RP) compound La6Ni5O16. Optimized reduction condition endows La6Ni5O12 with a superconducting state that exhibits onset transition temperature of ~ 18 K, as verified by both zero resistance and diamagnetic shielding effect. Pronounced hysteresis loops revealed by magnetization and torque magnetometry demonstrate the occurrence of vortex pinning. Specific heat measurements on a polycrystalline pellet of La6Ni5O12 reveal a clear superconducting transition at ~18 K and a superconducting volume fraction of ~ 25%, which strongly supports the presence of bulk superconductivity. Our results establish an unprecedented bulk sample platform for investigating superconductivity in nickelates at ambient pressure, which paves the way for further experimental studies into the superconducting mechanism.
summary: This paper reports the successful synthesis and characterization of bulk superconducting nickelate $	ext{La}_6	ext{Ni}_5	ext{O}_{12}$ at ambient pressure. Using multiple advanced measurements, the authors confirm a superconducting transition at $\sim 18$ K, establishing a crucial new platform for fundamental research into the mechanism of high-temperature superconductivity in this class of correlated materials.
main_problem: The primary challenge was realizing and understanding bulk superconductivity in nickelate superconductors, which are promising analogs to cuprates but have historically been limited to thin films or high-pressure conditions.
main_result: The authors successfully reported the first realization of bulk superconductivity at ambient pressure in the quintuple-layer square-planar nickelate La6Ni5O12, exhibiting an onset transition temperature of approximately 18 K.
method: The study employed a combination of synthesis techniques (topotactic reaction from a precursor) and multiple characterization methods, including transport (resistivity), magnetic (magnetization, torque), and thermodynamic (specific heat) measurements.
model_or_system: The physical system is the quintuple-layer square-planar nickelate La6Ni5O12. The research focuses on the electronic and superconducting properties of this material, which is structurally related to high-Tc cuprates.
key_observables: Superconducting onset transition temperature (Tc $\approx 18$ K), superconducting volume fraction ($\approx 25\%$), upper critical magnetic field ($\mu_0H_{c2}$), and the superconducting energy gap ($\Delta = 3.6$ meV).
important_parameters: Ambient pressure, annealing temperatures ($310^\circ	ext{C}$ to $320^\circ	ext{C}$), and oxygen stoichiometry.
main_assumptions: The superconducting state is highly sensitive to oxygen stoichiometry and annealing conditions, suggesting that precise control over the crystal structure is crucial for high-$T_c$ superconductivity.
figures_summary: Figures likely show structural evidence (XRD, STEM) confirming the phase transition, and plots detailing the temperature and field dependence of resistivity, magnetization, and specific heat anomalies.
paper_structure: The paper follows a structure of establishing the scientific gap (lack of bulk ambient-pressure samples), detailing the synthesis and structural characterization of the material, and then presenting multiple, consistent experimental measurements (transport, magnetic, specific heat) to confirm the superconducting state and characterize its parameters.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles the fundamental problem of high-Tc superconductivity in a correlated electron system, providing a new, accessible platform for studying mechanisms analogous to those in cuprates.
